title: Definition
body_md: Let $X$ be a variety (not necessarily smooth) and $\varphi\in\ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(X)$, then we say that {\it $\varphi$ has empty fixed locus} if $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\langle\varphi\rangle}(X):=\left\{x\in X\mid\varphi^t(x)=x,\,\,\mbox{for each}\,\, t\in\mathbb{Z}\right\}$ is empty.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Observe that this means that the automorphism itself has no fixed points but powers of $\varphi$ might have fixed points, and this is what will happen in many situations in this paper.

label: Lefschetz_number
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{Lefschetz_number}
    Let $Y$ be a CY manifold and let $v_Y$ be its volume form. Assume that $\varphi\in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(Y)$ is an automorphism of finite order $k$ with empty fixed locus. Then $\varphi^*v_Y=(-1)^{\dim Y+1}v_Y$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_\varphi(Y)=\emptyset$, we obtain that the Lefschetz number $L(\varphi)$ is zero and so by the holomorphic Lefschetz fixed-point formula we have
\begin{align*}
    0=L(\varphi)=\sum_{j=0}^{\dim Y}(-1)^{j}Tr\,{\varphi^{*}}(\overline{H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^{j})}).
\end{align*}
Since $Y$ is a CY manifold, we have that $H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^{j})=0$ for all $0<j<\dim Y$. Then
\begin{align*}
    0&=Tr\,{\varphi^{*}}(\overline{H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^{0})})+(-1)^{\dim Y}\, Tr\,{\varphi^{*}}(\overline{\underbrace{H^0(Y,\Omega_Y^{\dim Y })}_{{=\, \ensuremath{\mathbb{C}} \cdot \bar v_Y}}})\\
    0&=1+(-1)^{\dim Y}\,\bar \varepsilon, \quad \text{where } \varphi^*v_Y=\varepsilon\cdot v_Y.
    \end{align*}
    This finally gives
$$   
\varepsilon=\bar\varepsilon=(-1)^{\dim Y+1},
$$ 
so that $\varphi^*v_Y=(-1)^{\dim Y+1}v_Y$.

label: Enriques_manifold_index2
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{Enriques_manifold_index2}
Let $X$ be an Enriques manifold of Calabi--Yau type, that is $X=Y/\langle\varphi\rangle$
where $Y$ is a CY manifold, $\varphi\in\ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(Y)$ is an automorphism of finite order
$k$ with empty fixed locus, and $\pi\colon Y\to X$ is a quasi-étale cover. Then $\pi$ is
in fact \'etale, the order of $\varphi$ is $2$, and $X$ has index $2$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $X$ is smooth, $\pi$ is \'etale by \cref{rational_klt}~$(ii)$ and hence
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(Y)=\emptyset$ for all $1\leq s\leq k-1$. Then, writing
$\varphi^*v_Y=\varepsilon\, v_Y$ this gives $\varepsilon^s=(-1)^{\dim Y+1}$ for all
$1\leq s\leq k-1$, by \cref{Lefschetz_number}. Note that $\varepsilon=-1$ when $s=1$, since otherwise
\cref{log_enriques_CY_type}~$(iii)$ would give that $X$ is a CY variety. Assume now that
$k\geq 3$. Then $s=2$ lies in the above range and yields $1=\varepsilon^2=-1$, which is a
contradiction. Therefore $k=2$ and $X$ has index $2$ by \cref{log_enriques_CY_type}~$(ii)$. See also \cite[Proposition $2.1$, $(2)$]{BNWS} for a proof using the holomorphic Euler characteristic.

label: fixed_points_2
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{fixed_points_1}, the locus of fixed points of $\varphi$ on $M$ is the disjoint union of the non-empty sets $F_\ell(m_\varphi)$, over  those $\ell \in \mathbb{Z}/k\mathbb{Z}$ with  $\#L_\ell(m_\varphi) \geq n-d+1$. We count the connected components of each $F_\ell(m_\varphi)$ separately.
   
   Assume first that $\#L_\ell(m_\varphi) > n-d+1$. Again by \cref{fixed_points_1}, $F_\ell(m_\varphi)$ is a GFM of positive dimension $\#L_\ell(m_\varphi) + d - n - 1 \geq 1$, hence irreducible by \cref{connected_irred}, and in particular connected. Therefore $c_\ell = 1$.

   Now, assume that $\#L_\ell(m_\varphi) = n-d+1$. Then $F_{\ell}(m_\varphi)$ has dimension $\#L_{\ell}(m_\varphi) + d - n - 1 = 0$, so it is a  finite set of isolated points, each of which is its own connected component. We show that $\#F_{\ell}(m_\varphi) = k^{n-d}$, so that $F_{\ell}(m_\varphi)$ contributes exactly $c_{\ell} = k^{n-d}$ connected components. We establish this claim by applying B\'ezout's theorem, as follows. 
   
 
   
   Write $L_{\ell} (m_{\varphi}) = \{i_1,\ldots,i_{n+1-d}\}$ and introduce new coordinates $y_1 = x_{i_1}, \ldots, y_{n+1-d} = x_{i_{n+1-d}}$ for the variables whose indices belong to $L_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})$. Since $\#L_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})= n+1-d$, then  $$\widetilde{F}_{\ell}(m_{\varphi}) \cong \mathbb{P}^{\#L_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})- 1} = \mathbb{P}^{n-d},$$ with homogeneous coordinates $[y_1:\cdots:y_{n+1-d}]$.
   
   The variety $M$ is defined in $\mathbb{P}^n$ by exactly $n-d$ homogeneous equations of degree $k$ (see \eqref{equation_Fermat}):
   \begin{equation}\label{eq:system}
   \sum_{j=1}^{d} \lambda_{i,j}\, x_j^k + x_{d+1}^k + x_{d+2+i}^k = 0, \qquad i = 0, 1, \ldots, n-d-1,
   \end{equation} 
   where we put $\lambda_{0,j} = 1$ for all $j$. Upon restricting to $\widetilde{F}_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})$ (that is, setting $x_i = 0$ for all $i \notin L_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})$), each equation in \eqref{eq:system} becomes a homogeneous polynomial of degree $k$ in the variables $y_1, \ldots, y_{n+1-d}$. We thus obtain a system
   $$g_0(y_1,\ldots,y_{n+1-d}) = 0,\ \ldots,\ g_{n-d-1}(y_1,\ldots,y_{n+1-d}) = 0$$ 
   of $n-d$ equations of degree $k$ in $\mathbb{P}^{n-d}$, whose solution set is precisely $F_\ell(m_{\varphi}) = \widetilde{F}_{\ell}(m_{\varphi}) \cap M$. 
   
   
   We verify that this system is a zero-dimensional complete intersection in $\mathbb{P}^{n-d}$, i.e., that the $n-d$ hypersurfaces $\{g_i = 0\}$ intersect in finitely many points. Indeed, since $\Lambda \in X_{n,d}$, the $n+1$ hyperplanes are in general position, which means that every $(d+1)\times(d+1)$ minor of the matrix of coefficients $M(q_1,\ldots,q_{n+1})$ is nonzero. This general position condition ensures that the restrictions $g_0,\ldots,g_{n-d-1}$ form a regular sequence in the polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[y_1,\ldots,y_{n+1-d}]$, so their common zero locus in $\mathbb{P}^{n-d}$ has dimension $$\dim \mathbb{P}^{n-d} - (n-d) = (n-d) - (n-d) = 0\,,$$ as required.
    
    Since we have $n-d$ hypersurfaces of degree $k$ in $\mathbb{P}^{n-d}$ forming a zero-dimensional complete intersection, B\'ezout's theorem gives that their intersection consists of exactly $k^{n-d}$ points counted with multiplicity. Since $M$ is nonsingular and the intersection is transverse at every point (again by the general position condition on $\Lambda$), the fixed locus is also smooth and all multiplicities are equal to $1$, so $F_\ell(m_{\varphi})$ consists of exactly $k^{n-d}$ points. 
    
    Each of these $k^{n-d}$ points is an isolated point of $F_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})$, hence a connected component. Therefore $F_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})$ contributes with $c_{\ell} = k^{n-d}$ connected components as we wanted to show. Combining both cases gives the formula.

title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{condition_CY}
    Let $n\geq d+1$, $d\geq 2$ and $k\geq 2$. Assume that $M$ is a GFM of type $(d;k,n)$. Then, $M$ is a Calabi--Yau manifold  if and only if $k(n-d)-n-1=0$.

title: Proof
body_md: The "if" direction is \cite[Proposition~$2$, $(3)$]{HHAL}. For the converse, it follows from a direct computation using the adjunction formula and the properties of the Hodge numbers of complete intersections in the projective space.

body_md:
The definition of $\varphi$ shows $\#L_{\ell}(m_{\varphi})=t< n-d+1$, for each $\ell=0,\ldots, k-1$ and so by \cref{fixed_points_1}, we obtain that $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_\varphi(M)=\emptyset$.

If $\psi$ is another automorphism with empty fixed locus such that there is an $l\in \{0,\dots,k-1\}$ with $\#L_l(m_\psi)<t$. Now, since $n+1=tk$ by the Calabi--Yau condition, there exists an $l'\in\{0,\ldots, k-1\}$ such that $\#L_{l'}(m_\psi)>t$. This contradicts the fact that $\psi$ has empty fixed locus (see \cref{fixed_points_1}).

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that by \cref{order} the automorphism $\varphi$ has order $k$. If we assume that $k$ is prime, then we have $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$ is empty for every $s\in S$ (see \cref{fixed_points_prime}). Hence, $\pi:M\to M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is an étale morphism proving $(i)$.

    On the other hand, if $k$ is not a prime number then we obtain that $\ensuremath{\operatorname{codim}}(\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M))\geq 2$ for every $s\in S$ (see \cref{def_normal_variety}), then $\pi:M\to M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is a quasi-\'etale morphism.

label: quotients_log-enriques_CY
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that by \cref{order} the automorphism $\varphi$ has order $k$. By \cref{quasi_etale_morphism}, the quotient map $\pi\colon M\to M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is quasi-étale, so \cref{log_enriques_CY_type} applies. If $d$ is even, part $(ii)$ gives that $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is a Log Enriques variety of CY type and index two, and if $d$ is odd, part $(iii)$ gives that it is a CY variety.

For smoothness, by \cref{rational_klt}~$(ii)$ the quotient $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is smooth if and only if $\pi$ is \'etale, and by \cref{fixed_points_prime} this happens if and only if $k$ is prime. This equivalence holds for any $d$. In particular, if $d$ is odd, then $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is a CY manifold if and only if $k$ is prime, which proves $(ii)$. If $d$ is even, then $k$ is even by \cref{k_d_odd}~$(i)$ (see also \cref{log_enriques_CY_type}), so $k$ is prime if and only if $k=2$. This completes the proof of $(i)$, which is consistent with \cref{Enriques_manifold_index2} and \cref{Enriques_manifold} below.

label: stab
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{stab}
Let $q \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$ where $s$ is the index of $q$, then
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}(q) = \langle \varphi^s \rangle$. In particular the quotient
$M/\langle \varphi \rangle$ is locally isomorphic near $\pi(q)$ to $\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d / \langle \varphi^s
\rangle$ at the origin, where $\pi : M \to M/\langle \varphi \rangle$ is the
quotient map.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The inclusion $\langle \varphi^s \rangle \subseteq \ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}(q)$ follows from the definition of $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$. For the other inclusion, let $\varphi^j(q)=q$ for any $1 \leq j \leq
k - 1$, and set $\ell := \gcd(j, k)$. Note that $\ell\geq 2$, otherwise if $\ell = 1$ then \cref{fixed_points_prime} gives $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^j}(M) = \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi}(M) = \emptyset$, contradicting $\varphi^j(q) = q$. 
Hence $\ell \in S$, and again by \cref{fixed_points_prime}, we obtain that $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^j}(M) = \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ell}}(M)\neq\emptyset$. In particular
$q \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ell}}(M)$ with $\ell \in S$.

Now, we show that $s \mid \ell$. Since $q \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M) \cap
\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ell}}(M)$ with $s, \ell \in S$, if $\gcd(s, \ell) = 1$ then
\cref{fixed_points_in_others_divisors},~$(ii)$ gives $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M) \cap
\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ell}}(M) = \emptyset$, contradicting $q$ lying in both. Hence
$\gcd(s, \ell) \neq 1$, and in particular $\gcd(s, \ell) \in S$ divides both
$s$ and $\ell$. By minimality of $s$, we have $s \leq \gcd(s, \ell)$ and since $\gcd(s, \ell)$ divides $s$,
we obtain $\gcd(s, \ell) = s$, that is, $s \mid \ell$.

Therefore $s \mid \ell = \gcd(j, k)$ and $\ell \mid j$, which means $\varphi^j \in \langle
\varphi^s \rangle$. This shows $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}(q) \subseteq \langle \varphi^s \rangle$,
completing the proof of the first claim.

Finally, we know that $M$ is smooth at $q$ and $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}(q) = \langle
\varphi^s \rangle$ acts linearly on the tangent space $T_q M \cong \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d$,
by \cite[Section~$3.17$ and Claim~$3.17.1$]{Kollar_Sing} we have the isomorphism
\begin{align*}
    \left(M/\langle \varphi \rangle,\, \pi(q)\right)
    \;\cong\;
    \left(\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d/\langle \varphi^s \rangle,\, 0\right)\,. 
\end{align*}
head: environment

label: stab_subgroup
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{stab_subgroup}
Let $s\in S$ and let $q\in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{s(q)}}(M)$, where $s(q)$ is the index of $q$. Then
\begin{align*}
    \ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\langle\varphi^s\rangle}(q)
        =\left\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\right\rangle .
\end{align*}
Moreover $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))$ divides $k$, so either $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))\in S$ or $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))=k$. If $s\in S$, then
$q\in\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}}(M)$ and $M/\left\langle\varphi^s\right\rangle$ is locally isomorphic near $\pi(q)$ to
$\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d/\left\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\right\rangle$ at the origin. If $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))=k$, the stabilizer
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\langle\varphi^s\rangle}(q)$ is trivial and the image of $q$ is a smooth point
of $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By \cref{stab} the stabilizer of $q$ in the full group is
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\langle\varphi\rangle}(q)=\langle\varphi^{s(q)}\rangle$. Since
$\langle\varphi^s\rangle\subseteq\langle\varphi\rangle$, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\langle\varphi^s\rangle}(q)
        =\left\langle\varphi^s\right\rangle\cap\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\left\langle\varphi\right\rangle}(q)
        =\left\langle\varphi^s\right\rangle\cap\left\langle\varphi^{s(q)}\right\rangle
        =\left\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\right\rangle
\end{align*}

As $s$ and $s(q)$ both divide $k$, so does $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))$. Moreover $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))\geq s>1$, so either
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))\in S$ or $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))=k$. If $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))=k$ then $\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\rangle$ is trivial, the
action of $\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ is free near $q$, and its image in the quotient is a smooth point.
If $\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))\in S$, then $s(q)\mid\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))$ gives $\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}(q)=q$, so
$q\in\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}}(M)$. Since $M$ is smooth at $q$, the finite group
$\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}_{\langle\varphi^s\rangle}(q)=\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\rangle$ acts linearly on
$T_qM\cong\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d$, and by \cite[Section~3.17]{Kollar_Sing}, we obtain
\begin{align*}
    \bigl(M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle,\,\pi(q)\bigr)\;\cong\;\left(\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d/\langle\varphi^{\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))}\rangle,\,0\right)\,.
\end{align*}

label: terminal_singularities
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{terminal_singularities}
  Let $M$ be a Calabi--Yau GFM of type $(d;k,n)$. Assume that $k\geq 2$ and $(d,k)\not=(2,4)$. Assume that $\varphi\in H$ is an automorphism of $M$ with empty fixed locus. Then $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ is smooth if and only if $k$ is a prime number, and otherwise it has terminal singularities. The same statements hold for every quotient $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ with $1\leq s\leq k-1$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Recall that by \cref{order} the automorphism $\varphi$ has order $k$. The assertion about the smoothness of the quotients is given in \cref{quotients_log-enriques_CY}. Now, assume that $k$ is not a prime number that means that $S$ is non empty. Let $s \in S$ and $q \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$. 
By \cref{rmk:diagonalization}, the action of $\varphi^s$ on $T_qM \cong \ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^d$ can be diagonalized as
$$
\varphi^s=\ensuremath{\operatorname{diag}}(1,\ldots,1,\xi^{\sigma_1},\ldots,\xi^{\sigma_{d-v_s}})
$$
where $\xi$ is a primitive $o(\varphi^s)$-th root of unity, $v_s=\dim\left(\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)\right)$, and $1\leq\sigma_i\leq o(\varphi^s)-1 $ for every $i$. We can assume that the the smallest residue mod $o(\varphi^s)$ is $[\sigma_i]=\sigma_i$ for all $i=1,\ldots d-v_s$. 
This gives:
$$
\alpha^s_1:=\frac{1}{o(\varphi^s)}\sum_{i=1}^{d-v_s}\sigma_i\geq \frac{d-v_s}{o(\varphi^s)}=\frac{t(k-s)}{k}s\geq \frac{ts}{2}\,,
$$
since $d=t(k-1)-1$, $v_s=t(s-1)-1$ and $(k-s)/k\geq \frac{1}{2}$. We distinguish two cases:\\
{\bf Case 1}. If $ts>2$ then $\alpha^s_1>1$.\\
{\bf Case 2}. If $ts=2$, the only possibility is $t=1$ and $s=2$, since we are assuming that $S$ is non empty. Then, we obtain $\frac{2(k-2)}{k}\geq 1$. If we assume that
$\frac{2(k-2)}{k}=1$, then $k=4$ and we get $d=2$, which is not possible by assumption.
Therefore $\frac{2(k-2)}{k}>1$ and thus $\alpha^s_1>1$.\\
One can then repeat a similar computation for $j=2,\dots ,o(\varphi^s)-1$, since the action of $(\varphi^s)^j$ can be diagonalized locally in the same way, and we get that all the ages $\alpha^s_j>1$. 

Finally, by \cref{stab}, we have that $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Stab}}(q)=\langle\varphi^s\rangle$, for every $q \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$ whose index is $s\in S$. Hence, 
$(M/\langle\varphi\rangle, \pi(q))$ is isomorphic to $(\mathbb{A}^{d}/\langle\varphi^s\rangle, 0)$ and thus the singularity of $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ at $\pi(q)$
coincides with that of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^{d-v_s}/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ at the origin, which is terminal by the
above computations and by \cref{age}. Since $\varphi$ has empty fixed locus, the singular points of
$M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ arise only from $\ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^s}(M)$, where $s\in S$.
We conclude that $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ has terminal singularities whenever
$(d,k)\neq(2,4)$.

The same conclusion holds for each quotient $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ with $s\in S$. Indeed, by
\cref{stab_subgroup}, for a point $q\in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Fix}}_{\varphi^{s(q)}}(M)$ where $s(q)$ is its index, the stabilizer of $q$ in $\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ is
$\langle\varphi^{\gamma}\rangle$ with $\gamma=\ensuremath{\operatorname{lcm}}(s,s(q))$, and we have two cases:
\begin{itemize}
    \item [$(i)$] If $\gamma=k$, then $\langle\varphi^{\gamma}\rangle$ is trivial and the image of $q$
    is a smooth point of $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$.
    \item [$(ii)$] If $\gamma\in S$, then the singularity of $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ at $\pi(q)$
    is isomorphic to that of $\ensuremath{\mathbb{A}}^{d-v_{\gamma}}/\langle\varphi^{\gamma}\rangle$ at the origin. Its $\ensuremath{\operatorname{age}}$ can be computed in the same way as before with $\gamma$ in place of $s$, so $\alpha^{\gamma}_j>1$ for all $1\leq j\leq o(\varphi^{\gamma})-1$ whenever $(d,k)\neq(2,4)$. Hence $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$
    has terminal singularities whenever $(d,k)\neq(2,4)$.
\end{itemize}
Finally, for every $1\leq s\leq k-1$ we have $\langle\varphi^s\rangle=\langle\varphi^{\gcd(s,k)}\rangle$ with $\gcd(s,k)=1$ or $\gcd(s,k)\in S$, so $M/\langle\varphi^s\rangle$ equals either $M/\langle\varphi\rangle$ or $M/\langle\varphi^{\gamma}\rangle$ for some $\gamma\in S$. This concludes the proof.

label: lem:primitive_cohomology_complete_intersections
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:primitive_cohomology_complete_intersections}
    Let \(X\subset \mathbb{P}^{n}\) be a smooth complete intersection with \(\dim X={d}\). The restriction morphism \(\iota^k\colon H^k(\mathbb{P}^{n},\mathbb{Z})\to H^k(X,\mathbb{Z})\) is an isomorphism for any \(k\not= d\), and it is injective for \(k=d\).

label: lem:Betti_2_Hilbert_scheme
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:Betti_2_Hilbert_scheme}
    The second Betti number is given by \(b_2(S^{[n]})=b_2(S)+1\), for \(n\geq 2\).
head: environment

title: Example
body_md: Following \cite[Theorem 3.1]{OS}, we consider an Enriques surface \(E\) and denote by \(X=E^{[n]}\) its Hilbert scheme of $n$ points for some \(n\geq 2\). The universal cover \(Y\to X\) has degree \(2\) and \(Y\) is a CY manifold, hence \(X\) is an Enriques manifold of CY type and index \(2\).
head: environment

title: Example
body_md: Following \cite[6.1.5]{LogEnriques}, we let \(Y'\subset \mathbb{P}^{4n+1}\) be the CY manifold of dimension \(\dim Y'=2n\) obtained as smooth complete intersection of \(2n+1\) general quadrics of the form \(Q(x)+Q'(y)\), where \(x\) denotes the first set of \(2n+1\) coordinates and \(y\) the remaining ones. The involution \(\varphi\in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(Y')\) obtained as multiplication by \(-1\) on \(x\) is fixed-point-free, and it hence gives an Enriques manifold of CY type and index \(2\) as quotient \(Y'\to X'=Y'/\langle\varphi\rangle\). For a particular choice of quadrics, \(X'\) can be obtained as a quotient of a CY type generalized Fermat manifold as in \cref{Enriques_manifold}, see also \cref{subfamily_E}.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: Let \(X=S^{[n]}\) be the Hilbert scheme of \(n\geq 2\) points on a smooth projective surface \(S\), and let \(X'\) be the free quotient of a smooth complete intersection of dimension \(2n\). Then \(X\) and \(X'\) are not deformation equivalent.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Observe that \(b_2(X)=b_2(S)+1>1\) by \cref{lem:Betti_2_Hilbert_scheme} and the fact that \(b_2(S)>0\) since \(S\) is projective. On the other hand, if \(X'=Y'/\langle\varphi\rangle \) for \(\varphi\in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(Y')\), then \(H^*(X',\mathbb{Q})\cong H^*(Y',\mathbb{Q})^{\varphi^*}\) where the right hand side denotes the space of \(\varphi^*\)-invariant classes. This implies that \(b_2(X')\leq b_2(Y')=1\) by \cref{lem:primitive_cohomology_complete_intersections} (notice that equality is in fact attained whenever \(\varphi\) is restriction of a projective transformation). This immediately gives \(b_2(X)\not =b_2(X')\), implying that \(X\) and \(X'\) cannot be deformation equivalent by Ehresmann's Lemma.

label: cor:not_deformation
title: Corollary
body_md:
\label{cor:not_deformation}
    The Hilbert scheme \(X=E^{[n]}\) of \(n\geq 2\) points on an Enriques surface \(E\) and the free quotient \(X'\) of a smooth complete intersection of dimension \(2n\) of quadrics by an involution (as in \cite[6.1.5]{LogEnriques}) are not deformation equivalent.
head: environment

title: Proposition
body_md: The universal cover \(Y\to X=E^{[n]}\) of the Hilbert scheme of \(n\geq 2\) points on an Enriques surface \(E\), which is a projective CY manifold by \cite[Theorem 3.1]{OS}, is not deformation equivalent to a complete intersection.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: Since the morphism \(Y\to X\) is \'etale, of degree \(2\) by \cref{Enriques_manifold_index2}, there is an involution \(\varphi \in \ensuremath{\operatorname{Aut}}(Y)\) such that \(X=Y/\langle\varphi\rangle\). We have \(H^*(X,\mathbb{Z})\cong H^*(Y,\mathbb{Z})^{\varphi^*}\), which implies \(b_2(Y)\geq b_2(X)=11\) by \cref{lem:Betti_2_Hilbert_scheme} and the fact that \(b_2(E)=10\) for an Enriques surface. For a complete intersection \(Y'\) we have \(b_2(Y')=1\) by \cref{lem:primitive_cohomology_complete_intersections}, and since \(b_2(Y')\not=b_2(Y)\) we deduce that \(Y'\) and \(Y\) cannot be deformation equivalent.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: The universal cover of \(E^{[2]}\) is explicitly described by Hayashi in \cite[Proposition 2.6]{hayashi2015universal} as a blow-up of a quotient of \(S^{2}\), where \(S\to E\) is the K3 universal cover of the Enriques surface. Its Hodge numbers are computed in \cite[Theorem 6.1]{hayashi2015universal}. For \(n>2\), only a birational model of the universal cover of \(E^{[n]}\) is provided by Hayashi.

label: thm:dimension_deformation_space
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm:dimension_deformation_space}
The deformation spaces of $E^{[n]}$ and of $X'$ have dimension respectively $10$ and $(2n-1)(2n+1)^2+1$ (recall $\dim X'=\dim E^{[n]}=2n$).
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md:
Observe that for $n=1$ we obtain the dimension of the deformation space of Enriques surfaces which is $10$ in both cases. 
Interestingly the dimension of the moduli space is independent on $n$ in the first case and dependent in the second case.

title: Remark
body_md: We finish discussing the Morrison--Kawamata cone conjecture as formulated in \cite{PS} and in \cite{Gachet}. Observe that the Picard number of the Calabi--Yau manifold complete intersection and of its quotient, the Enriques manifold, is equal to one so that the Morrison--Kawamata cone conjecture trivially holds for both, the Calabi--Yau manifold and its Enriques quotient. In the case of the Enriques manifold $E^{[n]}$ and  of its universal Calabi--Yau cover the Picard number is bigger and the proof of the conjecture is open to our knowledge.
